references.text: Eliezer praises God for showing faithfulness (chesed) and guiding him rightly – this is the direct answer to the prayer in verse 12 where he asked God to show chesed toward Abraham.
Eliezer repeats his request for a sign to identify the right woman for Isaac, mirroring his original prayer in verse 12.
Nehemiah asks that God would let him succeed ('hatslicha na') – a parallel to Eliezer's prayer that God would make what is right happen on his journey ('haqreh na lefanay').
David's call to commit one's way to the Lord and trust in Him reflects Eliezer's confidence and prayer for God's guidance.
Jesus' teaching about prayer and God's willingness to answer His children can be seen in light of Eliezer's prayer and how faithfully God answered him.
The same prayer in the same event; verse 42 confirms and completes the introduction in verse 12.
A parallel prayer to Abraham's God that God's promise of kindness would be fulfilled for the descendant.
Confirmation that the prayer's request for guidance (v.12) has been fulfilled (v.48).
God's revelation as 'the God of Abraham' to confirm His presence and blessing upon the descendant.
God's identity as 'the God of Abraham' links Eliezer's prayer to the same divine plan revealed to Jacob.
Eliezer's prayer for God's goodness (v.12) is based on Abraham's obedience as described in verse 17.
Both prayers ask for God's 'kindness and faithfulness' (hesed) based on loyalty toward His servants.
Eliezer's prayer based on Abraham's faithfulness (v.12) is a practical expression of the faith that Paul describes in verse 29.
